body:
## Problem / why
Direct database queries and file reads bypass security checks, risking cross-tenant memory leakage and inconsistent writes.

## Goal & value
Build the central Memory Orchestrator as the single governed gateway for all memory operations with strict tenant and project ACL enforcement.

## Reference Documents
- `docs/Product_Forge_Agent_Memory_Architecture_Integration.md#section-7`
- `docs/Product_Forge_Agent_Memory_Architecture_Integration.md#section-14`

## In scope
- Unified gateway interface (Put, Get, Search, Delete, Validate, Consolidate).
- Multi-tenant isolation and Row-Level Security (RLS) enforcement.
- Project and user ACL boundary checks.
- Negative penetration tests verifying zero cross-tenant leakage.

## Out of scope
- Direct bypass of the orchestrator by individual agent workers.

## Definition of Done
- Leakage penetration tests pass with zero cross-boundary exposure.

## Verification
Structured `acceptance_criteria` is the single source of truth for verification.

design_pack.evidence_substitution: Gate 2 replaces design-only evidence with per-control test-run artifacts; design evidence is not delivery proof.
design_pack.concurrency_idempotency: Put is idempotent by record ID for the same tenant/project/owner. Cross-tenant/project ID reuse is denied. The orchestrator is stateless and race-tested under concurrent boundary load.

NIT: Logic Duplication: The simultaneous existence of `core/memory_orchestrator.py` and `go/pfmemory/orchestrator.go` suggests logic drift and unclear component ownership.
MAJOR: Observability (CL-010): No definition for telemetry, metrics, or logging of intercepted operations and ACL denials, preventing auditability of the security gateway.
Availability (Checklist 2): Design lacks a failure-mode definition (e.g., fail-closed) and circuit-breaking logic for when the underlying storage provider is unreachable.
MINOR: Dry-run Mode (Checklist 4): Destructive operations like 'Delete' and 'Consolidate' lack a mandatory dry-run/report mode to bound the blast radius of automated operations.
Reversibility (Checklist 1): No verified backup or state-reversal path is defined for the 'Consolidate' operation, which may destructively modify memory history.
BLOCKER: Language Rule Violation: "Build the central Memory Orchestrator" constitutes new shipped logic; implementation in `core/memory_orchestrator.py` violates the Go-only requirement for new logic.
Security Posture (CL-011): Design fails to specify or enforce the runtime role posture (NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS), which is mandatory to ensure RLS integrity and prevent bypass.
Parameterized Binding (CL-013): Missing requirement for constant-time token comparison and strictly parameterized tenant binding in the gateway interface to prevent leakage.
SUMMARY: The design establishes a critical security gateway but violates core engineering standards regarding language selection and mandatory security postures (RLS).
Top risks include potential RLS bypass due to undefined role permissions and a total lack of operational observability for security events.

NIT: All three ACs cite the same evidence artifact and candidate_sha a9425dfd; Gate 2 must replace these with distinct per-suite test evidence (partially acknowledged in pack learnings).
Audit "safe record ID" retention/redaction policy is unspecified while privacy_compliance is marked N/A; a short retention statement would close the gap.
MAJOR: AC-1 "all operations" is unenforceable as designed: only go/edpsvc call sites are wired, with no stated arch-test/static check proving no other code path reaches go/memory or datastore directly (bypass is merely out_of_scope, not prevented).

Authorization-vs-mutation ordering for Delete is ambiguous: C-3 says deletes "verify tenant, project, and ACL after repository access"; the design must pin read-verify-then-delete (or tenant-filtered delete) or a cross-tenant row could be mutated before denial.

Search result post-filtering is unspecified: the rls_tenant section rechecks "after every single-record read" only, yet AC-2/coverage claim filters "on every operation" — per-hit tenant/project/ACL revalidation of multi-record Search results must be explicit.

Search bound contradicts the approved NFR: NFR says k <= 100 and performance says default 20, but config_contract allows PF_MEMORY_MAX_SEARCH_K = 1..1000 with default 100; the contract cannot be met as written.
MINOR: RLS role-posture test runs only "when a test DSN is configured"; without a required CI DSN the CL-011 NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS evidence is silently skipped.

PF_MEMORY_PRINCIPAL contract is internally contradictory (precedence "server" vs env key; empty→"deny in production" vs default→"existing server principal"); precedence and production-empty behavior need one rule.
AC-3's "four negative leakage suites" are not enumerated as four distinct named tests; C-4 lists TestLeakageSuites as both negative_test and positive_test.
D-1 hides legacy project-empty rows with no migration owner/ticket and no metric for filtered-out rows, so silent data invisibility is undetectable in production.
Rollback trigger "roll back on denial spikes" has no threshold, alert, or lead-time defined (checklist 2 availability).
No statement that pfmemory metrics reuse the existing edpsvc metrics registry/namespace; duplicate metric definitions would break dashboards (checklist 10 reuse).
SUMMARY: Design is now Go-only, fail-closed, and observability-aware; prior blockers are properly dispositioned. Top risks: AC-1 has no anti-bypass enforcement, delete/search authorization ordering and per-hit filtering are not pinned, and the k-bound NFR contradicts the config contract. Resolve the MAJOR items before Gate 1.5; no BLOCKERs remain.

NIT: All three ACs still cite the same single evidence artifact docs/MEMORY-ORCHESTRATOR-DESIGN.md with an identical candidate_sha a536d6d1; distinct per-suite Gate 2 test evidence remains to be substituted (prior NIT reopened with the new sha).
MAJOR: PF_MEMORY_MAX_SEARCH_K default/empty is "100" while NFR, quotas, and performance_capacity all pin default 20; prior finding was dispositioned ACTIONED ("default 20") but the delta still ships 100 — contract contradicts the approved NFR as written.
PF_MEMORY_OP_TIMEOUT valid range is "positive duration <= 30s" while NFR states "operation timeout <= 5s"; a 30s configured value would violate the approved bound yet pass startup validation.
MINOR: controls and implementation_controls are byte-identical duplicated rows (7 controls twice) in the same delta; two maintained copies will diverge at Gate 2 evidence updates — keep one or state they are mirrored.
design_pack.contracts.files omits go/pfmemory/bypass_test.go while affected_files and review_scope.files include it; the contract file list is the one Gate 2 traces.
No control row maps CL-011 runtime role posture (NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS) to a check/symbol/test, although risks and rls_tenant reference a required role-posture test with PF_TEST_MEMORY_DSN.
SUMMARY: Delta correctly actioned the prior ordering, search-revalidation, bypass-test, metric-reuse, and rollout-threshold findings; the security model (server-resolved Scope, read-verify-delete, per-hit revalidation) is coherent and Go-only per language rule.

Top risks: two config/NFR contradictions (search default, timeout ceiling) that make the approved contract unenforceable as written, and duplicated control rows that will drift during evidence collection.
No blocker; recommend fixing the two config-vs-NFR mismatches and de-duplicating control rows before Gate 1.5.

NIT: Prior NIT disposition appears wrong: traceability and ac_evidence still give all three ACs the single evidence artifact docs/MEMORY-ORCHESTRATOR-DESIGN.md with identical candidate_sha a536d6d1; per-suite Gate 2 test evidence not yet substituted.
MAJOR: No control row maps the DoD-required "edpsvc handler tests prove wiring": C-2 applies_to go/edpsvc/main.go but every cited test lives in go/pfmemory/orchestrator_test.go, and go/edpsvc/main_test.go appears in no control, traceability, or test_matrix row — AC-1/AC-2 edpsvc evidence would be unmapped at Gate 2.
MINOR: FR-1 traceability.test lists only go/pfmemory/orchestrator_test.go although FR-1 verification and DoD require "go test ./... in go/edpsvc"; traceability omits the second package.

Controls C-1/C-2/C-3/C-5 cite concurrency_test TestConcurrentCrossBoundary, which appears in no FR verification, suite list, or traceability row (FR-3 pins only TestConcurrentBoundaryLoad); dangling or duplicated test reference.

functional_spec.observability lists only memory_ops_total, memory_denied_total, memory_op_duration_seconds, omitting memory_filtered_projectless_total that control C-5 and risk D-1 depend on; the two changed sections disagree on the metric contract.
SUMMARY: Delta correctly fixes the prior config contradictions (default 20, 5s cap), declares the controls mirror, adds bypass_test to contracts.files, and adds C-8 role-posture control; no blocker.

Top risks: unmapped edpsvc wiring test evidence for AC-1/AC-2, a dangling TestConcurrentCrossBoundary reference, and metric-contract drift on memory_filtered_projectless_total between functional_spec and controls.

NIT: Prior NIT disposition text does not address its finding (traceability/ac_evidence still give all three ACs the single artifact docs/MEMORY-ORCHESTRATOR-DESIGN.md with identical candidate_sha a536d6d1); DEFERRED is acceptable for Gate 1.5 but the disposition wording is mismatched.
C-7 static bypass test lives in go/pfmemory while enforcing go/edpsvc behavior; ensure CI always runs go/pfmemory tests on any edpsvc change, or the guard silently weakens.
MINOR: FR-2/AC-2 traceability and coverage still omit go/edpsvc/main_test.go; the handler-level denial test TestMemoryCrossTenantDenied is now attached only under C-9 (AC-1), so AC-2's edpsvc boundary evidence remains unmapped to its own AC.
AC-2 coverage test string is bare `go test ./...` with no package scope, unlike AC-1 (`in go/pfmemory`, `in go/edpsvc`); evidence of which package proves AC-2 is ambiguous.

C-2 is `applies_to: go/edpsvc/main.go` with `owner: go/pfmemory`, yet all four cited tests live in go/pfmemory; cross-package evidence/ownership for an edpsvc-file control is inconsistent with C-9's pattern.

C-3 read-verify-delete has a verify-then-delete window; design should pin that the DELETE itself carries tenant/project predicates (or equivalent atomicity) so TestConcurrentBoundaryLoad cannot mutate a row that changed between verify and delete.
SUMMARY: Delta correctly actioned the prior MAJOR/MINORs: C-9 added, FR-1 traceability includes go/edpsvc, dangling TestConcurrentCrossBoundary reference removed, and memory_filtered_projectless_total restored to observability; no blockers found.
Top residual risks: AC-2/FR-2 edpsvc evidence still not mapped to AC-2, and read-verify-delete atomicity under concurrent load needs an explicit tenant/project-scoped DELETE invariant.
Guardrails otherwise satisfied: Go-only logic, C-8 role posture (CL-011), rollback defined, bounded metrics, no schema migration.

NIT: The C-7 disposition ("Gate 2 will attach per-suite evidence") still does not address the original NIT about ensuring go/pfmemory tests run on any edpsvc change; disposition/finding mismatch persists.
Delta design_pack carries both `controls` and `implementation_controls` as full duplicates (acknowledged mirror); long-term drift risk—consider deriving one at render time.
MAJOR: review_scope.components excludes "go/dualvec storage implementation" while controls C-10 and review_scope.files include go/dualvec/*.go; AC-2's SQL/storage-filter guarantee therefore rests on a control in an explicitly excluded component, making the AC-2 storage path unverifiable within the declared scope.
MINOR: Residual from prior C-2 fix: row now has applies_to=go/pfmemory/orchestrator.go but symbol still go/edpsvc/main.go:memoryHandle; control file/symbol/owner remain internally inconsistent.

go/dualvec/pg_store.go is in affected_files/contracts.files but no control, test, or symbol row references it; C-10 names only sqlite_store.go:DeleteScoped despite claiming "SQLite and PostgreSQL" predicates.
C-4 symbol `TestLeakageSuites` is not among the four named suites listed in its own control text or test_matrix AC-3; confirm the aggregator exists or re-point the symbol.
AC-3 coverage row lists test names under `failure_cases`, unlike AC-1/AC-2 rows which list failure modes; the delta field is inconsistent within itself.
SUMMARY: Delta is largely consistent with the prior ACTIONED dispositions; AC-1/AC-2 traceability, package-scoped tests, and ScopedDeleter atomicity are now reflected in the design rows.
Top risks: AC-2's storage-filter control sits in an excluded component, and the pg_store path plus C-2's symbol/applies_to mismatch leave residual evidence gaps for the leakage guarantees.
No blocker-level AC, security, or data-loss defect found in the changed fields; Gate 1.5 can proceed once the scope/control-row mismatches are reconciled.

NIT: Delta still carries `controls` and `implementation_controls` as byte-identical full duplicates despite the prior disposition "Resolved in revised design"; drift risk persists — derive one at render time.
MAJOR: AC-2's "SQL/storage filters guarantee zero cross-tenant and cross-project leakage" is only controlled at the storage layer for Delete (C-10/C-11/C-12); no control row covers scoped Get/Search predicates in go/dualvec or go/edpdata, so read/search leakage guarantees rest solely on orchestrator post-read revalidation (C-2), not on storage filters as the AC states.

C-7 (bypass enforcement) is owned by and lives in go/pfmemory/bypass_test.go but its control targets go/edpsvc call sites; a static check inside the pfmemory module cannot reliably see edpsvc's repository usage, and it will not run on edpsvc-only changes, weakening AC-1's "intercepts all operations" proof.
MINOR: C-8 check is `go test ./...` while its failure_behavior requires CI failure when PF_TEST_MEMORY_DSN is missing or role posture fails; the stated check does not encode that DSN/CI gate, so the role-posture invariant (CL-011) can pass vacuously outside CI.
AC-3 coverage row's `tests` is bare `go test -race ./...` with no package scope, unlike AC-1/AC-2 rows which specify "in go/pfmemory"/"in go/edpsvc"; ambiguous which module the race gate covers.
The prior NIT disposition "go/pfmemory tests run on any edpsvc change — Resolved in revised design" has no corresponding evidence in the delta design_pack; disposition appears unsubstantiated.
SUMMARY: Delta correctly actioned the component-scope, C-2 symbol, C-11/C-12 storage-delete, and AC-3 failure_cases findings; no blockers in the changed fields.
Top risks: AC-2 storage-level guarantee is delete-only (read/search storage filters uncontrolled), and the AC-1 bypass control is positioned where it cannot observe edpsvc call sites.
controls/implementation_controls duplication remains despite its "resolved" disposition; re-verify role-posture DSN gating and race-test package scope at Gate 2.

NIT: `controls` and `implementation_controls` remain byte-identical full duplicates in the delta; the prior disposition (go-modules gate) does not address duplication, so the drift risk stands.
C-4's check `go test -race ./...` lacks the "in go/pfmemory" package scope now present in the AC-3 coverage row.

functional_spec.outcome: A Go gateway governs every existing memory operation with server-resolved tenant/project/ACL enforcement and canonical validation.
functional_spec.rollback: Revert the gateway wiring and restore the prior edpsvc binary. No schema or stored-data mutation.
assumptions: Authenticated tenant/project/principal are resolved at the server boundary
Legacy project-empty rows are hidden by governed reads pending migration

requirements.auth: Scope and ACL are enforced server-side; caller authority fields are rejected on mismatch.
requirements.title: Govern every memory operation
acceptance: Given an authenticated memory operation, when it enters edpsvc, then it is validated, scoped, and routed through the orchestrator; a static test forbids direct repository bypass.
requirements.idempotency: Put is idempotent by record ID for the same tenant/project/owner.

requirements.auth: Tenant, project, ACLScope, and owner must match before any data or mutation is returned.
requirements.title: Deny cross-boundary access
requirements.trigger: Read, search, write, or delete targets another tenant/project or private owner.
acceptance: Given a cross-boundary request, when executed, then no data is returned or mutated; search revalidates every hit and delete is read-verify-delete.
requirements.idempotency: Denied operations have no side effects.

requirements.auth: All suites use server-resolved Scope only.
requirements.title: Prove leakage resistance under concurrency
errors: any exposure fails the test suite
outputs: all suites pass under race detector
requirements.trigger: Four negative leakage suites run concurrently.
acceptance: Given four negative leakage suites, when run concurrently with -race, then all pass with zero exposure.
requirements.data_rules: No test may bypass the orchestrator.
requirements.idempotency: Concurrent reads do not mutate state; writes use unique IDs.
verification: go test -race ./... in go/pfmemory; TestCrossTenantReadWriteSearch, TestCrossProjectReadWriteSearch, TestACLPrivateDenial, TestConcurrentBoundaryLoad
requirements.preconditions: Fake and real repository adapters are available in tests.

functional_spec.compatibility: Allowed response shapes preserved; project-empty rows hidden; delete requires ScopedDeleter support and fails closed otherwise.
functional_spec.observability: memory_ops_total, memory_denied_total, memory_op_duration_seconds, memory_filtered_projectless_total; reuse edpsvc registry; audit.
functional_spec.data_lifecycle: Existing memory rows are unchanged. Governed reads hide project-empty rows. New writes require project. No retention or schema change.
open_questions: None. D-1 strict project isolation is approved at Gate 1.

acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Memory Orchestrator intercepts and validates all memory reads, writes, and searches.
AC-2: SQL/storage filters guarantee zero cross-tenant and cross-project data leakage.
AC-3: Four negative leakage test suites verify boundary isolation under concurrent load.
